_how_to_fill: Fill each entry following references/writing-descriptions.md in the bi-joe-data-profiler skill. source: system_metadata | user_documentation | inferred | pending. When source is inferred, confidence (high|medium|low) and evidence are required. The description is plain business language that says more than the name does. A column name may appear in plain text where it helps, never in backticks. grain builds on it ('One row for each ...'). Suggest BEAM annotations in beam{} following references/beam-annotations-guide.md. Then run: bijoe check <dir> and bijoe render <dir>.

dataset.summary: Operational data of a company that manufactures and sells bicycles, parts and accessories. It covers its customers and stores, sales and purchasing, production work, products and employees. The orders and transactions run from the middle of 2022 to the middle of 2025.
evidence: Product categories are Bikes, Components, Clothing and Accessories (4 categories, 37 subcategories)
Sales orders (31,465) run from 2022-05-30 to 2025-06-29 and purchase orders (4,012) from 2022-04-15 to 2025-09-21
Work orders start between 2022-06-02 and 2025-06-01
Employees were hired between 2006 and 2013 (290 rows)
71 tables in 6 schemas: dbo, HumanResources, Person, Production, Purchasing and Sales

dbo.AWBuildVersion.description: Current version number of the AdventureWorks 2025 sample database.
dbo.AWBuildVersion.grain: One row for each recorded version of this sample database; the table holds a single row, so it only describes the version that is installed
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
dbo.AWBuildVersion.ai_notes: The column Database Version has a space in its name, so it must be quoted in queries. VersionDate (2025-10-06) and ModifiedDate (2025-11-14) are different dates, although the source comments describe both in nearly the same words.

beam.table_why: Only one row and one key (SystemInformationID), with no validity dates or version history, so only the current value is kept.

Database Version.why: The version number is the whole purpose of the table, so every row needs it.

dbo.DatabaseLog.description: Audit table tracking all DDL changes made to the AdventureWorks database. Data is captured by the database trigger ddlDatabaseTriggerLog.
dbo.DatabaseLog.grain: One row for each change made to the structure of the database, such as creating a table or index, with the exact statement that was run
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
dbo.DatabaseLog.ai_notes: All 927 rows were posted within about four minutes on 2025-11-14 (13:01 to 13:05), and 58% are CREATE_EXTENDED_PROPERTY events, which fits the one-off creation of this sample database and its documentation rather than ongoing activity. DatabaseUser is dbo in every row. XmlEvent holds 584 distinct values for 927 rows, so several changes share one event record.

beam.table_why: One time column (PostTime) and each row is finished once the change has happened: 927 rows, none updated later.

PostTime.why: The moment the change happened; every row has one.

DatabaseUser.why: The user who ran the change; the value is dbo in all 927 rows.

Event.why: The kind of change decides whether Schema and Object are filled: they are empty in 1.19% and 2.37% of rows, which fits events that are not about one object.

dbo.ErrorLog.description: Audit table tracking errors in the the AdventureWorks database that are caught by the CATCH block of a TRY...CATCH construct. Data is inserted by stored procedure dbo.uspLogError when it is executed from inside the CATCH block of a TRY...CATCH construct.
dbo.ErrorLog.grain: One row for each error that was caught and logged by the database's error handling, with the time, user, error number and message
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
dbo.ErrorLog.ai_notes: The table has 0 rows, so no value, range or distribution could be measured. Everything here is based on the column names and the source system comment.

beam.table_why: Column design only, because the table is empty: a single ErrorTime and no later milestone columns, which is how a log of finished events looks.

ErrorTime.why: The moment the error happened; the column is required.

HumanResources.Department.description: Lookup table containing the departments within the Adventure Works Cycles company.
HumanResources.Department.grain: One row for each department of the company; the 16 departments are placed into 6 department groups
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system

beam.table_why: One row for each DepartmentID with no validity dates, so only the current department list is held.

DepartmentID.why: The source system's identifier for each department.

Name.why: Required for every department; unique across the 16 rows.

GroupName.why: Every department belongs to a group (6 groups, none missing).

HumanResources.Employee.description: Employee information such as salary, department, and title.
HumanResources.Employee.grain: One row for each person who works or has worked for the company; all 290 rows are marked as currently active
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
HumanResources.Employee.ai_notes: OrganizationNode has a database type the engine could not read (shown as NULL), but its values look like paths such as /1/1/ and give the position in the reporting hierarchy; one employee has none (0.34%), which fits the top of the hierarchy. CurrentFlag is true for all 290 rows, so the table holds no former employees. ModifiedDate is a date for 287 rows and a date with time for 3.

beam.table_why: One row for each BusinessEntityID, with no validity dates or version columns, so only current values are kept. Earlier jobs and pay are in separate history tables.

BusinessEntityID.why: Identifies the employee and is the same number as the person's row in the person tables (measured: 290 of 290 found).

NationalIDNumber.why: A government-issued number people use to identify an employee; unique across 290 rows. Values are masked.

HireDate.why: A hire date should not change, and every employee has one.

BirthDate.why: A date of birth should not change.

VacationHours.why: A balance of hours available now, so it cannot be added up over time. The source comment says the unit is hours.

SickLeaveHours.why: A balance of hours available now, so it cannot be added up over time. The source comment says the unit is hours.

HumanResources.EmployeeDepartmentHistory.grain: One row for each period an employee spent in a department on a given shift; an employee and a start date together identify a row
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
HumanResources.EmployeeDepartmentHistory.ai_notes: EndDate is empty in 97.97% of rows (290 of 296), which matches one current assignment for each of the 290 employees; the other 6 rows are earlier assignments that ended between 2009 and 2013. A shift is stored on each assignment, so a change of shift inside the same department would be a new row.

beam.table_why: The same BusinessEntityID repeats (296 rows for 290 employees) with a StartDate and an EndDate, so earlier assignments are kept.

BusinessEntityID.why: Measured relationship: 296 of 296 values found in the employee table.

StartDate.why: The first day in the department; every row has one.

HumanResources.EmployeePayHistory.grain: One row for each pay rate that takes effect for an employee on a given date; an employee and the rate change date together identify a row
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
open_questions: Which currency is Rate in?
PayFrequency says salary is paid monthly or every two weeks, but Rate is described as hourly. Is the rate of a salaried employee converted to an hourly amount?
HumanResources.EmployeePayHistory.ai_notes: The comment on Rate calls it an hourly rate, and the values (6.50 to 125.50, median 14) fit an hourly amount. 14 values are above the upper limit of 41.19 measured for outliers. PayFrequency has only the values 1 (180 rows) and 2 (136 rows), described in the source as monthly and every two weeks.

beam.table_why: BusinessEntityID repeats (316 rows for 290 employees), each row with the date its rate took effect, so earlier rates are kept.

RateChangeDate.why: The date the rate starts; part of the key and never empty.

Rate.why: A rate, so it cannot be added up. The source comment calls it an hourly rate.

evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
HumanResources.JobCandidate.ai_notes: Only 2 of 13 rows (15.38%) have a BusinessEntityID, which matches the source comment that it is filled when the applicant was hired. Resume is XML in a Microsoft résumé schema and may hold personal details. 11 of 13 rows share the same ModifiedDate (2007-06-23).

beam.table_why: One row for each JobCandidateID with no dates beyond the last-changed date, so only the current state of the application is held.

BusinessEntityID.why: Filled only for hired applicants; both values found in the employee table (2 of 2).

Resume.why: Required, and every one of the 13 résumés is different.

HumanResources.Shift.grain: One row for each work shift, defined by a start time and an end time; the three 8-hour shifts together cover the whole day
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system

beam.table_why: Three rows, one per ShiftID, with no dates or versions.

ShiftID.why: The source system's identifier for each shift.

SpatialLocation is a geography value the engine could not read as a type; it was masked because its coordinates showed up as a possible card number in the checks. AddressLine2 is empty in 98.15% of rows. ModifiedDate is a date for most rows, but 1,851 rows carry the same date and time (2024-12-20 10:09:29), which looks like one bulk update.

beam.table_why: One row for each AddressID with no validity dates. Sales orders point to this table twice, as billing address and as shipping address (BillToAddressID and ShipToAddressID, both found 100%), so one table plays two roles.

AddressID.why: The source system's identifier for each address.

AddressLine1.why: An address needs a street line; none is missing. Values are masked.

Person.BusinessEntity.ai_notes: 20,777 identifiers equals 19,972 people plus 701 stores plus 104 vendors (the row counts of those tables), so each identifier belongs to exactly one of the three kinds. The ModifiedDate values all fall within about 30 minutes on 2017-12-13.

beam.table_why: One row for each BusinessEntityID with no descriptive columns, dates that change or versions.

BusinessEntityID.why: The shared identifier that the person, store, vendor and employee tables all reuse (measured: every value in those tables is found here).

Person.BusinessEntityAddress.ai_notes: Only 3 of the 6 address types are used (2, 3 and 5). 18,774 rows use type 2. ModifiedDate is a date for 19,324 rows and a date with time for 290.

beam.table_why: A link between BusinessEntityID and AddressID with an address type: 35 entities have more than one address (19,579 entities, 19,614 rows).

AddressID.why: Measured relationship: 19,614 of 19,614 values found; each address is used by one row only.

PersonID is unique across all rows, so no person is a contact for two entities. The relationship from PersonID to the person table was not detected by the engine, but its source comment names the person table.

beam.table_why: A link between BusinessEntityID (the store or vendor) and PersonID with a contact type; 82 entities have more than one contact (805 entities, 909 rows).

EmailAddressID.why: The identifier of the e-mail address row itself; unique and one-to-one with the person.

EmailAddress.why: The point of the table; never empty. Values are masked.

Person.Password.grain: One row for each person who has sign-in credentials, holding a salted hash of the password and the salt
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
Person.Password.ai_notes: The hash and the salt are security data and are masked by the engine. The source comment on PasswordHash says it is the password for the e-mail account.

beam.table_why: One row for each person (BusinessEntityID unique, 19,972 rows) with no history, so only the current credential is kept.

PasswordHash.why: Required for every row; unique. Values are masked.

PasswordSalt.why: Required for every row; unique. Values are masked.

Person.Person.description: Human beings involved with AdventureWorks: employees, customer contacts, and vendor contacts.
Person.Person.grain: One row for each human being known to the company, whether employee, customer, store contact or vendor contact; PersonType tells which
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
Person.Person.ai_notes: PersonType is IN (individual customer) for 18,484 of 19,972 rows, SC (store contact) for 753, GC for 289 and EM (employee) for 273, according to the values and the source comment. Title is empty for 94.95% of rows and Suffix for 99.73%. NameStyle is false in every row. Demographics is XML with a survey; AdditionalContactInfo is XML and is filled for only 10 rows. The Person table's ModifiedDate has one date that covers 44.2% of rows.

beam.table_why: One row for each BusinessEntityID with no validity dates or version columns.

BusinessEntityID.why: The identifier shared with the business entity table; unique.

FirstName.why: Never empty in 19,972 rows. Values are masked.

LastName.why: Never empty in 19,972 rows. Values are masked.

PersonType.why: Never empty; 6 different values, 92.55% of them IN.

Person.PersonPhone.description: Telephone number and type of a person.

evidence: Table comment stored in the source system

beam.table_why: BusinessEntityID is unique across 19,972 rows and there are no validity dates, so only one current number is kept for each person.

PhoneNumber.why: The point of the table; never empty. Values are masked.

Person.PhoneNumberType.description: Type of phone number of a person.
Person.PhoneNumberType.grain: One row for each kind of telephone number a person can have; the three kinds are cell, home and work
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system

PhoneNumberTypeID.why: The source system's identifier for each phone number type.

Person.StateProvince.grain: One row for each state or province of a country or region, with the sales territory it belongs to
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
Person.StateProvince.ai_notes: StateProvinceCode is text and 9 values have leading zeros, so it must not be converted to a number. 96 of 181 rows are in one country (FR), which is more than half. For 8 rows IsOnlyStateProvinceFlag is true: the code is not available and the country code is used.

beam.table_why: One row for each StateProvinceID with no dates or versions.

StateProvinceID.why: The source system's identifier for each state or province.

StateProvinceCode.why: The code people use for a state or province; unique across 181 rows.

Production.BillOfMaterials.description: Items required to make bicycles and bicycle subassemblies. It identifies the heirarchical relationship between a parent product and its components.
Production.BillOfMaterials.grain: One row for each component used in a parent product during a period, with the quantity needed; the parent, the component and the start date together identify a row
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
Production.BillOfMaterials.ai_notes: EndDate is empty in 92.57% of rows, so most component lines are still in use. All start and end dates fall in 2021. 96.23% of the quantities are in unit EA. The engine did not detect ProductAssemblyID and ComponentID as relationships, but the source comments name the product table for both.

beam.table_why: Parent (ProductAssemblyID) and child (ComponentID) are both products, BOMLevel gives the depth, and 103 rows with BOMLevel 0 have no parent: a parent and child hierarchy of products.

ProductAssemblyID.why: The parent product. Empty for the top level (103 rows, equal to the number of rows with BOMLevel 0).

ComponentID.why: The product used as a component.

StartDate.why: Required; part of the unique combination.

Production.Culture.description: Lookup table containing the languages in which some AdventureWorks data is stored.
Production.Culture.grain: One row for each language (with an optional country) in which product descriptions are stored; one row is the neutral language
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
Production.Culture.ai_notes: CultureID is empty (12.5%, one row of 8) in the profile. That row is the invariant language, whose code is blank text; it is not a missing value. Codes are padded with spaces to 6 characters.

beam.table_why: Eight rows, one per CultureID, with no dates or versions.

CultureID.why: The source system's identifier (a short language code) for each language.

Production.Document.grain: One row for each folder or document in the product maintenance document tree, placed in the tree by DocumentNode
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
open_questions: Does FolderFlag true mean a folder? The source comment says 1 is a document, but the rows with true have no file and no file extension.
Production.Document.ai_notes: FolderFlag appears reversed against its comment (0 = folder, 1 = document): the 4 rows with FolderFlag true are the same number as the rows with no FileExtension (33.33%) and no Document file (33.33%), which looks like folders. DocumentNode has a type the engine could not read (shown as NULL); the values look like tree paths such as /1/1/. FileExtension is .doc for all 8 rows that have one.

beam.table_why: One row for each DocumentNode with no validity dates; Revision and ChangeNumber show the current version only.

DocumentNode.why: Position of the item in the document tree; unique across 12 rows.

Production.Illustration.grain: One row for each drawing that shows how part of a bicycle is assembled, stored as XML
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
Production.Illustration.ai_notes: Diagram is XML text exported from a drawing program, between 16,441 and 41,804 characters per row. IllustrationID runs from 3 to 7, so 2 identifiers in the range are not present.

beam.table_why: Five rows, one per IllustrationID, with no dates or versions.

IllustrationID.why: The source system's identifier for each illustration.

Production.Location.grain: One row for each place in the factory where products are made or stored, with the hourly cost and the working hours it has available
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
open_questions: Do the 7 locations with a cost rate and an availability of 0 hold stock only, with no manufacturing?
In which currency is CostRate?
Production.Location.ai_notes: 7 of 14 rows have a CostRate of 0.00 and 7 have an Availability of 0.00. This looks like places where stock is kept but no manufacturing takes place, but the data does not say so.

beam.table_why: One row for each LocationID with no dates or versions.

LocationID.why: The source system's identifier for each location.

CostRate.why: An hourly rate, which cannot be added up.

Availability.why: A capacity level, not to be added over time. The source comment says it is in hours.

Production.Product.description: Products sold or used in the manfacturing of sold products.
Production.Product.grain: One row for each product, whether a finished item the company sells, a part it makes itself or a part it buys
evidence: Table comment stored in the source system
open_questions: Why is DiscontinuedDate empty for every product, while SellEndDate is filled for 19.44% of them?
In which currency are StandardCost and ListPrice?
Production.Product.ai_notes: 200 products have both a StandardCost and a ListPrice of 0.0000. Size is text with both numbers and codes (such as 44 and S), and is empty for 58.13% of rows. DaysToManufacture is 0 for 246 rows. 55 prices lie above the outlier limit of 1,412.

beam.table_why: One row for each ProductID with start and end dates of selling but no history of earlier values; price and cost history is in separate tables.

ProductID.why: The source system's identifier for each product.

ProductNumber.why: The code people use for a product, such as AR-5381; unique across 504 rows.

FinishedGoodsFlag.why: ProductSubcategoryID and ProductModelID are empty in 209 rows, the same number as the rows where this flag is false (209), so the flag appears to decide whether they apply.

StandardCost.why: A cost of one unit, which cannot be added up.

ListPrice.why: A unit price, which is always non-additive.

evidence: Table comment stored in the source system

beam.table_why: Four rows, one per ProductCategoryID, with no dates or versions.

beam.table_why: One row for each product and location pair, with no date column that would make it a series, so only the current stock is held.
